text:
maria_support: Customer reported intermittent 401s right after they rotated keys. They pasted a curl and the Authorization header looks like a cookie rather than an API key. attaching their sanitized snippet and the response we saw.

maria_support: ```
curl -i -H "Authorization: ApiKey session=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsIn...; Path=/; HttpOnly" \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key not found or malformed","trace_id":"trace-7a9c"}
```

jordan_support: Can you paste the raw header we logged and the trace id from the backend? Any SDK/client version info?

maria_support: Trace id: trace-7a9c. Client: webapp v4.5.2 using our web-sdk@1.2.3. Raw header captured in request logs: ```Authorization: ApiKey session=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly```

maria_support: Customer says they call our client with `credentials: 'include'` and a custom auth helper. Their note: "we pass token from cookie into the header".

lee_engineer: I reproduced this locally — the customer's helper appears to concatenate `document.cookie` instead of reading the token value. Example buggy code: ```js
// buggy
const authHeader = `ApiKey ${document.cookie}`;
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: authHeader }, credentials: 'include' })
```
This results in the header containing `session=...; Path=/` which our server treats as a single malformed key -> 401 invalid_api_key.

lee_engineer: Short-term triage: ask customer to set header to the raw key string (no cookie prefix) or read cookie value by splitting on `;` and extracting the `session` value. Example fix: ```js
// safe extraction
const token = document.cookie.split(';').map(s => s.trim()).find(s => s.startsWith('session='))?.split('=')[1];
if (token) fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `ApiKey ${token}` } });
```

maria_support: I sent that snippet to the customer as a workaround. Also recommended disabling `credentials: 'include'` while they test.

lee_engineer: I'll add a sanitizer in web-sdk to strip common cookie prefixes and raise a warning. Opening ISSUE-1234 to track SDK patch and also adding a server-side heuristic to log when an authorization header contains `;` or `Path=` so support can triage faster.

deploy-bot: web-sdk@1.2.4-beta.1 published (contains header sanitizer, tests).

jordan_support: Customer applied the token-extract workaround and confirmed requests are now 200. They rotated again to be safe. Closing on our side, leaving ISSUE-1234 open for the SDK/server improvements. :white_check_mark:
